newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says free trade area won't hurt revenue.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says free trade area won't hurt revenue.

text.p: The ASEAN Free Trade Area will not hurt government revenue, the national news agency Bernama quoted Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar as saying on Monday.

The customs union that the Association of South East Asian Nations is evolving over the next decade would increase government revenue through excise duties collected from locally-made goods, Affifudin said after a signing ceremony.
"AFTA... encourages the growth of local industries and this would enable the (Malaysian) government to collect more excise duties from locally manufactured goods," Bernama quoted Affifudin as saying.

Six ASEAN members -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam are committed to slashing most import tariffs to five percent or less by 2003. Vietnam has until 2006 and Burma, Cambodia and Laos, which join the grouping next month, will have until 2008.
